title.en: IoT and the Web of Things

body.en: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of devices, each with embedded hardware and software, that can sense, collect and exchange data over the Internet. Smart TVs, smart watches, smart bulbs, home security cameras and connected cars are examples. The *Web of Things* (WoT) uses ordinary web technologies, such as web pages and web services, to connect and control these devices, so they can be accessed from any browser.

points.en: IoT devices sense, collect and share data
Examples: *smart* watch, smart bulb, connected car
WoT: web standards to access IoT devices from a browser

title.en: On the board: How the Internet of Things connects

say.en: In the Internet of Things, everyday devices have sensors and a network connection.
They send their data through a Wi-Fi router or mobile network.
Over the Internet the data reaches the cloud, where it is stored and analysed.
A phone app reads the data and can send commands back: switch off the bulb, lock the car.
Inside a smartphone, sensors measure movement and position.
Many such sensors across a city make a smart city: smart traffic lights, parking and waste bins.

body.en: A sensor detects a change in its surroundings, such as light, temperature, motion or tilt, and sends the information to a processor. A smartphone has an accelerometer that senses tilt and movement (to rotate the screen or count steps), a gyroscope for orientation, a proximity sensor that turns the screen off near your ear, and an ambient light sensor. A smart sensor also processes the data before sending it. A smart city uses such *sensors*, IoT and data analytics to manage traffic, water, electricity, waste and safety efficiently.

points.en: Accelerometer: tilt and movement; step counting, screen rotation
Proximity sensor: screen off during calls
Smart city: smart traffic lights, water meters, waste bins with fill *sensors*

problem.en: Explain how a smart traffic signal in a smart city could work.

steps.en: Sensors or cameras at the junction count vehicles on each road.
The data is sent over the Internet to a control system.
The system analyses the counts and gives a longer green light to the busier road.

answer.en: Sensors collect traffic data, IoT sends it, and analytics adjusts the signal timing.
